para.text: A possible use of 2D graphs is so-called Data Tracking (or: Data Tracing). This means that the graph is being used to obtain information about the original input data and not mere the converted screen co-ordinates. An application can be to click a point on the screen and retrieve the original X and Y values in full resolution.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;

para.text: Such an application requires access to the original X and Y values, and possible also to the relation between them. This is probably not complete impossible to implement in XYGraph but t it will require interpreting all the plotting commands that are called and to retrieve the required information from that. This is beyond the concept of XYGraph (see however the exception at the end of this screen).

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: However the application that does call XYGraph (that means the one you are writing) has all the information available, as it may be assumed that all X and Y data are stored in some way. Therefore I have assumed that Data Tracking must be implemented from the overall application, and XYGraph offers aids to facilitate this, notable the export records. For easy data tracking the shape of the ruler can be changed and snapping can be used, see

para.text: The following example shows how to use the export records to implement real-time data tracking triggered by the mouse move. XYExportD is set initially to enable to see if actual co-ordinates have been read (if the mouse is clicked outside a graph area nothing happens). You can expand this example, for example by enable data-tracking only if the Alt-key is pressed as well.
